problem:
Find the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)={e}^{2x}$ at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ is
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=1$ is given by

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1)+\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}(x-1)^{2}.
$$

The coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is

$$
\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}.
$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=1.$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1)=4{e}^{2\cdot 1}=4{e}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}=\frac{4{e}^{2}}{2}=2{e}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
